title: Tensor product commutes with finite products
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $t\ge0$ an integer, $P_1,\dots,P_t$ and $N$ $R$-modules, and $\prod_{k=1}^tP_k$ the product module (componentwise operations). Then there is a unique $R$-linear map $\big(\prod_{k=1}^tP_k\big)\otimes_RN\to\prod_{k=1}^t(P_k\otimes_RN)$ with $(x_k)_k\otimes y\mapsto(x_k\otimes y)_k$, and it is an isomorphism of $R$-modules.

source.place: standard property of the tensor product (tensor product commutes with finite direct sums, which for finitely many factors are the products), used in More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second proof, where H_1(M,f) ⊗_R S = H_1(M ⊗_R S, f) is asserted for flat S
